message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
My provisional reading is **sinus rhythm at about 75–80 beats/min**, with prominent T waves in the front chest leads. I would want clinical context before calling this normal.

- **Rhythm:** Regular, with a P wave before each QRS.
- **Conduction:** PR interval appears normal and QRS complexes are narrow; no obvious bundle branch block.
- **Axis:** Mildly leftward.
- **Voltage:** Large QRS complexes in several chest leads. This can occur as a normal variant; voltage alone does not establish heart enlargement.
- **ST–T changes:** Tall, fairly symmetric T waves in **V2–V3**, with slight depression/upsloping of the preceding ST segments. No definite conventional ST-elevation pattern is apparent.

The anterior ST–T changes deserve attention if this ECG was taken for chest pain. More pronounced upsloping ST depression with tall symmetric T waves can indicate an acute coronary blockage—the **de Winter pattern**—but this image does **not clearly establish that diagnosis**. [Supporting research](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7507532/)

**If you currently have chest pressure, shortness of breath, sweating, faintness, or pain spreading to the arm or jaw, seek emergency care now.** Otherwise, have a clinician review this alongside a previous ECG and your symptoms; repeat ECGs and blood tests may be needed depending on the situation.

How old is the person, why was the ECG taken, and were there any symptoms at the time?
